bread_ration.name: bread ration
bread_ration.lore: Roman legionaries marched upon bucellatum, a bread twice baked that would outlast a campaign and could break a tooth, and this loaf is of the same old fashion. It may be eaten when soaked in water, though to eat it dry requires some hardihood. It fills the belly and keeps a delver walking, which is all that is asked of it.

dried_meat.name: dried meat
dried_meat.lore: By salt and smoke meat has been kept through winters and sieges since long before any wrote down the craft. These strips are wound tightly in waxed cloth that does not name the beast they came from, and though they are as tough to chew as bootlaces they sustain like a proper meal.

hard_cheese.name: hard cheese
hard_cheese.lore: When Odysseus and his men found the cave of the Cyclops stacked with racks of cheese they helped themselves before the master came home, and for such a cave-aged wheel as this the peril might have been well worth it. The rind is thick as bark, and the heart is dense, salty and good for a long march.

wild_mushroom.name: wild mushroom
wild_mushroom.lore: Foragers in the world above have a saying, that there are old mushroom hunters and bold mushroom hunters, but no old, bold ones. Yet in the dungeon's damp corners the pale caps that glow faintly at the gills are safe to eat, and they are filling and earthy and a mild restorative for small hurts.

apple.name: apple
apple.lore: Genesis gives no name to the fruit of Eden, and the apple was blamed for it only later, with some help from the Latin, in which malum means both 'apple' and 'evil'. This one is innocent of all harm, crisp and cold and wondrously fresh for such a depth, and it quiets hunger and leaves small hurts a little mended.

trail_rations.name: trail rations
trail_rations.lore: Seasoned delvers pack these waxed parcels of dried fruit, salted crackers, hard tack and a sealed jar of rendered fat. None has ever praised the taste, but no fare that fits in a satchel is more filling, and it never spoils.

healing_herb.name: healing herb
healing_herb.lore: Achilles, who learned the art from the centaur Chiron, is said to have packed his soldiers' wounds at Troy with yarrow, which for his sake is named Achillea, and monks grew it in their physic gardens to the same end. The bitter leaves, when they are chewed, do little for hunger but a great deal to staunch bleeding.

elvish_bread.name: elvish bread
elvish_bread.lore: Travellers are warned in the old tales never to eat at the table of the Fair Folk, since a single bite may keep a guest beneath the hill a hundred years. But it seems that this pale loaf was baked for the road and for no snare, and it is light as a wafer and faintly sweet, and one piece will carry a traveller farther than a full pack of rations.

hearty_stew.name: hearty stew
hearty_stew.lore: Esau came famished from the field and sold his birthright to his brother Jacob for a bowl of red lentil stew, and one who opens a sealed clay pot of this, still warm, may well understand him. It is thick with roots and tender meat, and it restores both strength and blood.

deep_fungi.name: deep fungi
deep_fungi.lore: Only in the lowest passages, where no light has ever fallen, do these mushrooms grow, feeding upon whatever seeps from enchanted stone. At the first bite the head begins to spin, but soon the body is steady and well fed, and it comes away subtly changed, a little stronger or quicker or sharper than it was before.

void_ration.name: void ration
void_ration.lore: On the floors of the abyss, where common food rots within an hour, are found these dark bricks of pressed provision, and by whom they are made no one knows. To eat one is to feel a cold and steady vigour fill the limbs and abide as true strength for battle, and hunger is forgotten for a long while after.

philosopher_tea.name: philosopher's tea
philosopher_tea.lore: The emperor Shennong, as the Chinese legend has it, was boiling water beneath a wild tree when a few leaves drifted into the pot and the draught pleased him, and sages have steeped leaves ever since. This violet tea is gathered near old ruins. It settles the mind and leaves it lastingly wiser, so that scholars say the hard questions seem to wait politely for an answer.

ambrosia.name: Ambrosia
ambrosia.lore: Doves carried ambrosia to Zeus, for it was the food of the gods of Olympus, and Homer speaks of it both as meat and as drink, and as the balm with which Thetis anointed dead Patroclus to keep his body from decay. It was never meant for mortal tongues, and a mortal who tastes it is fed, healed and bettered in every part.

golden_apple.name: Golden Apple of Hesperides
golden_apple.lore: Gaia gave to Hera for a wedding gift a tree that bore golden apples, and Hera planted it on the western edge of the world, with the Hesperides to tend it and the serpent Ladon coiled about the trunk. For his eleventh labour Heracles held up the sky while Atlas fetched three, and one bite of such fruit fills, heals and toughens the body for good.

peach_of_immortality.name: Peach of Immortality
peach_of_immortality.lore: Xi Wangmu, the Queen Mother of the West, has an orchard in heaven where these peaches grow, and the slowest of its trees ripen once in nine thousand years. Journey to the West tells how Sun Wukong, who was set to guard them, ate the best himself. A single one will mend the body and fill it, and leave behind some lasting gift.

tantalus_plum.name: Tantalus's Plum
tantalus_plum.unidentified_name: a perfect-looking fruit just out of reach
tantalus_plum.lore: Tantalus served his own son to the gods to learn whether they truly knew all things, and they knew what he had done. So he stands in the underworld in a pool that drains away when he stoops to drink, beneath boughs that lift their fruit when he reaches. This plum was gathered from those boughs, and though it heals deep wounds it is true to its tree and will barely touch your hunger.

magic_dungeon_carrot.name: Magic Dungeon Carrot
magic_dungeon_carrot.lore: This carrot, which glows faintly orange and smells of wildflowers, was grown in some enchanted bed far from any sun. It is perfectly good to eat, yet rumor holds that a certain magical beast deeper in the dungeon loves nothing better, so that a wise traveler will keep one in the pack against the day of that meeting.

starnut_tart.name: Starnut Tart
starnut_tart.lore: When the old miners went down the shafts they carried tarts like this one, baked of crushed starnuts and sweet apple in a crust of ration bread, and at night they shared them with the little cave folk who danced with them. It is golden on top and still faintly fizzy, it will keep for weeks in a pack, and it is a very pleasant thing to eat.

caviar.name: caviar
caviar.eat_line: Salty little pearls. Unexpected, but so right.
caviar.lore: A little jar of black caviar on crushed ice, found where nobody thinks to look, like a note tucked in the margins of an old and dusty book. Fancy food has no business this far down. On its own it is a rich, salty mouthful. Set beside something humble, it might be more.

tater_tots.name: tater tots
tater_tots.eat_line: No fancy words, no complicated plans. Just tater tots, and they are good.
tater_tots.lore: A wire basket of golden tater tots, somehow still crisp. Never one for fancy words or complicated plans, a tater tot is exactly what it looks like. On its own it fills a gap. Set beside something grand, who knows?
